title: Luke Slaughter of Tombstone
paragraphs: A late-era adult Western starring Sam Buffington as Luke Slaughter, a tough cattleman and former cavalry officer facing danger in Arizona Territory near Tombstone.

Late-era CBS adult Western starring Sam Buffington as former cavalryman turned Arizona cattleman Luke Slaughter, with Junius Matthews as Wichita. The frozen GRH set contains the complete sixteen-broadcast run; April 6 was pre-empted and a separate February 18 audition is outside the numbered broadcast run.
GRH documents the program through CBS run (February 23, 1958 to June 15, 1958) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Junius Matthews (performer on 16 recordings), Sam Buffington (performer on 16 recordings), William N. Robson (director on 16 recordings, producer on 16 recordings, radio adaptor on 1 recording, and writer on 1 recording), Tom Hanley (editorial supervisor on 8 recordings and sound patterns on 3 recordings), Wilbur Hatch (composer on 7 recordings, conductor on 6 recordings, and music on 4 recordings), Amerigo Moreno (conductor on 3 recordings, composer on 2 recordings, and music supervisor on 1 recording), and Fran Van Hartesfeldt (writer on 4 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include late network-radio drama, cattle ranching and cattle drives, Tombstone and Arizona Territory, adult radio Western, frontier law, violence and justice, and frontier business and cattle economy.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Post-Civil War Arizona Territory cattle frontier, Late-era CBS network radio Western, One-off OBrien Paints sponsorship, and April 6, 1958 pre-emption.
